method: Compared proportion-interval and repeated-look claims with the NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook and FDA adaptive-design guidance, and the zero-event interpretation with Hanley & Lippman-Hand; ran six offline assertions against all lesson Python fences and claims. No provider calls or historical experiment replay were performed.

observations.trace: Input validation rejects empty and invalid counts; Wilson and Clopper-Pearson reproduce boundary behavior; the p=.9 planning table matches; all-success IID one-sided lower-bound planning yields 59 trials; zero observed events are distinguished from zero risk; fixed-horizon decisions differ from pre-specified sequential monitoring; all Python fences run independently.

limitations: The 40/40 historical observation is preserved as a reported result; task-level dependence across eight tasks means the binomial interval is illustrative under an IID assumption and does not establish population success rate.
The arithmetic checks do not rerun the original provider/model calls, recover raw responses, or validate the historical task scoring.
The sample-size formula is a Wald normal approximation for a single proportion; it is neither a Wilson-width guarantee nor a power calculation for comparing versions.
No sequential experiment, multiplicity-controlled evaluation, provider call, or production-risk measurement was run.
